tool.name: ATRIUM OCR line quality
tool.description: sorts OCR text lines into Clear, Noisy, Trash, Non-text and Empty (needs a GPU)
tool.command: #if $models.source == 'staged': export HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 && export TRANSFORMERS_OFFLINE=1 && #set $model_name = str($models.model.fields.path) #else: export HF_HOME="\${_GALAXY_JOB_TMP_DIR:-\$PWD/tmp}/hf" && #set $model_name = '@QWEN@' #end if @PREPARE@ "CLASSIFY.MODEL_NAME=$model_name" "CLASSIFY.EXPECTED_LANGS=$expected_langs" "CLASSIFY.WORKERS_MAX=\${GALAXY_SLOTS:-1}" "CLASSIFY.INPUT_CSV=\$JOB/out/page_stats.csv" "CLASSIFY.TEXT_DIR=\$JOB/out/PAGE_TXT" "CLASSIFY.OUTPUT_LINES_LOG=\$JOB/out/LINE_CATEG" "AGGREGATE.RAW_LINES_CSV=\$JOB/out/LINE_CATEG" "AGGREGATE.OUTPUT_DOC_DIR=\$JOB/out/LINE_STATS" "AGGREGATE.OUTPUT_STATS=\$JOB/out/page_quality.csv" && @RUN@ && @COLLECT@ && mv out/LINE_CATEG/*.csv '$line_quality' && mv out/page_quality.csv '$page_quality' #if $method.kind == 'text-lines': && mv out/LINES/*.csv '$lines' #end if

param.name: expected_langs
param.label: Expected languages
param.help: ISO 639-3 codes, comma-separated, the first the main one. A line identified as another language is checked against these before it counts as noise.

validator.message: Three-letter codes separated by commas, for example ces,deu,eng

param.name: source
param.label: Perplexity model (Qwen2.5-0.5B)
param.option: Download it from the Hugging Face Hub in the job (about 1 GB)
Use the copy staged on this server

param.name: model
param.label: Staged model
param.help: Staged by an administrator with the data manager 'ATRIUM Hugging Face models'.

validator.message: No copy of Qwen2.5-0.5B is staged on this server.

tool.help:
**What it does**
Sorts every text line of an OCR document by how usable it is, so that the noise of a bad scan does not reach later stages. It runs all five stages of the ATRIUM OCR post-processor (`ufal/atrium-ocr-postprocess`_), release @TOOL_VERSION@: split, statistics, extract, then **classify** and **aggregate**.
**Needs a GPU.** The classifier measures each line's perplexity with the language model Qwen2.5-0.5B on CUDA, and stops (exit 1) on a runner without a GPU. For the CPU stages alone, use *ATRIUM OCR post-processing*.
**Categories**
- *Clear*: readable text in an expected language. - *Noisy*: readable, with OCR errors. - *Trash*: OCR garbage. - *Non-text*: numbers, symbols, page furniture. - *Empty*: nothing to read.
Each line is also identified by language (fastText) and checked against the *expected languages*.
**Inputs and reading methods**
As in *ATRIUM OCR post-processing*: one document per job, read as text lines (most formats, ALTO included), as ALTO with alto-tools, or as OCR JSON.
**Model**
Qwen2.5-0.5B (Apache-2.0) is downloaded in the job, or read from a copy an administrator has staged with the data manager *ATRIUM Hugging Face models*. The fastText language-identification model is in the image.
**Outputs**
- *Lines with their category* (CSV): one row per line, with ``categ``, ``quality_score``, the language and the measures behind the decision. - *Categories per page* (CSV): the number and share of lines of each category per page. - *Line table* (CSV, text lines only), *page texts*, *page statistics*, the *document record* and the *paradata*, as in *ATRIUM OCR post-processing*.
**Licence**
The code is MIT; the paradata lists each component's licence.
.. _`ufal/atrium-ocr-postprocess`: https://github.com/ufal/atrium-ocr-postprocess
